info.name: E-commerce Platform
info.description:
Gateway + all backing services (auth-service, product-service, inventory-service, eureka-server) for the Spring Boot microservices monorepo. Folders: Gateway (edge), Auth Service, Product Service, Inventory Service, Eureka Server — each with a client-facing (via gateway) flow and a direct-to-service section for local debugging.

Flow: run "Login" in Auth Service first — it captures `accessToken` into a collection variable and Postman's cookie jar picks up the `refresh_token` cookie automatically for the "Refresh Token" request. Product/Inventory write requests additionally need a CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role on the logged-in user — a VIEWER-only token gets 403 on those.

Event-driven note: product writes (POST/PUT/DELETE) publish to Kafka topic `product.events` after the write commits; inventory-service consumes it asynchronously and provisions/removes its own `inventory.stock_levels` row a moment later — a `GET /api/inventory` immediately after `POST /api/products` may still 404 until that catches up (prototype-scope, no synchronous coupling by design — see docs/architecture/design/HLD-event-driven-inventory.md).

item.name: Gateway
item.description: The platform's single public edge (:8080). Routes /api/auth/**, /oauth2/**, /.well-known/jwks.json to auth-service, /api/products/** to product-service, and /api/inventory/** to inventory-service (own inventoryCb circuit breaker). Requests below hit the gateway itself; use the service folders for the routed calls.

request.description: Internal circuit-breaker fallback path — not in PUBLIC_PATHS, so a direct call returns 401 unless it's an internal forward. Kept here for reference/documentation, expect 401.

item.name: Auth Service
item.description: Identity provider — password login, Google OAuth2 login, rotating refresh tokens, JWKS. All requests below go through the gateway (base path /api/auth). A "Direct (bypass gateway)" sub-folder hits auth-service on :8081 directly for debugging.

request.description: Public. Gated by auth.registration.enabled (default false — enable via AUTH_REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true). Always assigns ROLE_VIEWER server-side; no role field accepted. Returns 201 + UserResponse, no token (registration ≠ login).

Public. Returns 200 + TokenResponse { accessToken, tokenType, expiresIn, authMethod }. Sets HttpOnly refresh_token cookie (Path=/api/auth) — never in the JSON body. Enable Postman's cookie jar to carry it to Refresh/Logout. Captures accessToken into the collection variable on success.

Public, but requires the refresh_token cookie set by Login (cookie only — no header/body fallback). Rotates the refresh token: old one is invalidated, new Set-Cookie issued. Requires Postman cookie jar to be enabled for this domain.
Public, reads refresh_token cookie (missing is fine). Always returns 204. Clears the cookie.
Bearer JWT required. Returns UserResponse { id, email, emailVerified, displayName, status, roles[], createdAt }.

Bearer JWT required. Always introspects the caller's own bearer token (request body's token field is currently ignored). Returns ValidateResponse { valid, userId, email, roles[], authMethod, expiresAt }.
Public. Standard JWKS document (public RSA keys). Cache-Control: max-age=300, public.

Public. Redirects to Google's consent screen (302) — only 404s unless GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are configured. Not fully testable in Postman since it's a browser redirect dance (state/PKCE + callback to /login/oauth2/code/google); at most observe the 302 here. On success the browser is redirected to auth.oauth2.default-redirect-uri (dev: http://localhost:5173/auth/callback) with a token pair minted and the refresh cookie set, same as password login.

item.name: Product Service
item.description: Catalog service (Phase 1G). Reads (GET /api/products**) are PUBLIC — no authentication required. Writes (POST/PUT/DELETE) require Bearer JWT with CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role, and use optimistic locking (echo the `version` you last read on PUT, or get 409). Writes publish to Kafka topic `product.events` after commit — see Inventory Service folder for the consuming side. Requests below go through the gateway (base path /api/products). A "Direct (bypass gateway)" sub-folder hits product-service on :8082 directly.

request.description: PUBLIC — No authentication required (Phase 1G). page 0-based, size default 20 / max 100, sort default sku,asc (repeatable). Returns a Spring Data PagedModel<ProductResponse>: { content: [{id, sku, name, priceAmount, priceCurrency, active, lastKnownQuantity}], page: {size, totalElements, totalPages, number} }.
PUBLIC — No authentication required (Phase 1G). Path param id must be a UUID. Returns ProductResponse with images array populated; 404 problem+json if unknown, 400 if id isn't a valid UUID.

PUBLIC — No authentication required (Phase 1G). Returns ProductCatalogAggregateResponse: { product: ProductResponse, inventory?: {productId, quantity, reserved} }. Inventory lookup is fail-open (returns inventory: null if inventory-service is unavailable). 404 problem+json if product unknown.

Requires CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role. 201 + ProductResponse (includes `version`, starts at 0) on success; 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT on duplicate sku; 403 FORBIDDEN if the caller lacks the role. Publishes PRODUCT_CREATED to Kafka topic `product.events` strictly after the DB transaction commits. Captures the new id into the `productId` collection variable.

Requires CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role. `version` must match the value on the currently-persisted row (returned by Create/Get) or this returns 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT — optimistic locking, not a soft check. 200 + ProductResponse (with incremented version) on success. Publishes PRODUCT_UPDATED to Kafka after commit (inventory-service currently treats this as log-only — see docs/architecture/design/HLD-event-driven-inventory.md Open Question).

Requires CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role. 204 on success, 404 if unknown. Publishes PRODUCT_DELETED to Kafka after commit — inventory-service removes the matching inventory.stock_levels row (idempotent; no-op if it never existed or is already gone).

item.name: Inventory Service
item.description: Stock-level service, added by the event-driven inventory feature (docs/architecture/design/HLD-event-driven-inventory.md). Reads (GET) need any authenticated user; writes (POST/PUT/DELETE) need CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN, same as Product Service. Rows here are also provisioned/removed asynchronously by a Kafka consumer reacting to product.events — a direct POST here is for manual stock adjustments, independent of that pipeline. Requests below go through the gateway (base path /api/inventory). A "Direct (bypass gateway)" sub-folder hits inventory-service on :8083 directly.

request.description: Bearer JWT required. Returns a Spring Data PagedModel<InventoryResponse>: { content: [{id, productId, quantity, version}], page: {...} }.
Bearer JWT required. 404 problem+json if unknown.

Requires CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role. 201 + InventoryResponse on success; 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT if a row for this productId already exists (unique constraint — this is also the idempotency guard the Kafka consumer relies on). No FK to product.products (separate database) — this succeeds even for a productId that doesn't exist in the catalog, by design.

Requires CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role. `version` must match the currently-persisted row or this returns 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT (optimistic locking). 200 + InventoryResponse (incremented version) on success.
Requires CATALOG_MANAGER or ADMIN role. 204 on success, 404 if unknown.

item.name: Eureka Server
item.description: Service registry (:8761). Unauthenticated in dev (documented gap — needs Basic auth/mTLS before non-loopback exposure). No business API; useful for debugging service registration.

request.description: XML by default; Accept: application/json for JSON.
